rubrics: The response should list specific gimbal modes by name (e.g., Lock,  Pan Follow, Tilt Follow, FPV, Point-of-Interest / Orbit, ActiveTrack) and explain in one sentence how each mode affects which axes the gimbal holds or follows, so the user can choose the correct mode for circling around a subject.

The response should state concrete camera shooting settings needed for a hyperlapse. For example, recommended final frame rate (e.g., 24/25/30 fps), recommended shutter-speed rule (e.g., approximate 180° shutter: shutter = 1/(2×frame rate)), and example ISO/aperture/ND guidance for daylight, so the user can set exposure correctly while moving.

The response should give numeric guidance for interval/shot timing or recording method. For example, an example mapping of walking speed + radius → interval, so the user can choose a practical interval.

The response should identify which gimbal mode(s) are best for keeping the subject centred while circling. For example, Point-of-Interest / Orbit or ActiveTrack + Follow, and explain why each recommended mode maintains centering during an orbit, so the user understands the functional reason behind the choice.

The response should provide a concise, step-by-step setup checklist (with numbered steps) that the user can follow before shooting. For example, calibrate the gimbal, enable tracking/POI and set target, lock auto-exposure/white balance, set follow speed/smoothness, set intervalometer or video mode, and perform a short test orbit — each step clear and actionable so it is directly usable in the field.

The response should recommend example gimbal parameter values to try (follow speed / follow smoothness/responsiveness levels). For example, “Follow speed medium (3–5/10) and smoothness high (6–8/10),” and explain the trade-off between responsiveness and lagging/overshoot so the user can tune behavior to their movement style.

The response should advise practical movement technique that helps keep the subject centered (e.g., maintain a constant radius, steady pace, consistent camera height, use a visible marker on the ground or a fixed pivot point), including concrete numbers where helpful (e.g., keep ~2–5 m radius depending on subject size), so the user can coordinate walking with gimbal behavior.

The response should explain when to prefer shooting continuous stabilized video vs. shooting stills with an intervalometer for a hyperlapse, listing pros and cons for subject centering and post-processing (for example: stills allow precise frame-to-frame registration, video + stabilization allows realtime centering but may need speed ramping), so the user can pick the workflow that best preserves centering.

The response should describe common failure modes that cause the subject to drift off-center (e.g., tracking loss from occlusion, dynamic background, rapid camera rotation, tilt drift) and give at least one concrete mitigation per failure (e.g., widen tracking box, lower follow speed, lock exposure, increase smoothing), so the user can troubleshoot on the spot.

The response should include one or two short example configurations (scenario → settings) that are directly applicable, e.g., “Walking slowly around a person at ~3 m radius: POI/orbit mode, interval 1 s, 24 fps final, shutter ~1/50, follow speed 3/10” — For example, provide at least one human-scale and one small-object example to illustrate differences.

The response should instruct the user to perform a quick test pass and iteratively adjust settings (explicitly: do a 10–15 second test orbit, check centering and exposure flicker, then adjust follow speed/interval/exposure) so the user validates settings before committing to a full take.
